amicable

AM-ih-kuh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Amicable is friendly and free of hostility, especially describing an agreement, settlement, or relationship.

The divorcing couple surprised their lawyers by keeping the entire process amicable, splitting their shared bookstore's inventory over coffee instead of in court.

Example

After a season of on-court rivalry, the two tennis stars maintained an amicable relationship off the court, often practicing together in the off-season.

Amicable describes the tone of an interaction or relationship -- friendly and cooperative, especially notable when there was potential for conflict.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

cordial: Cordial describes real warmth of manner, especially in formal or professional dealings -- a cordial welcome or handshake has genuine friendliness in it. Amicable sets a lower bar for the relationship itself: an amicable settlement is simply free of hostility, even if nobody is being warm.

harmonious: Harmonious means actively in tune -- people living or working together smoothly, their wishes and efforts lining up. Amicable claims less: an amicable split or dispute stays friendly and free of ill will even between people who no longer agree on much.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

hostile: unfriendly and aggressive

acrimonious: bitter and full of ill will, especially in a dispute

Where it sits · how warm the relationship is — civil → amicable → close-knit

civil vs. amicable: Civil just means polite enough to avoid open conflict -- it doesn't carry the genuine warmth that amicable suggests.

close-knit vs. amicable: Close-knit goes even further than amicable, describing a bond that's warm and tightly connected, not merely free of conflict.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — amic-

root — amic-: friend (Latin amicus)

suffix — -able

suffix — -able: characterized by; tending to be (Latin -abilis)

Put it together

Put it together: Amicable comes from Latin amicus ('friend') -- the same root behind amity, which you already met earlier in this course. An amicable settlement or relationship is, at root, one carried out in a spirit of friendship rather than conflict.

Use the root in a new word: amity

Use the root in a new word: amity: Aunt Rosa raises a toast 'to amity' at every family dinner.

Root Check

Word Choice

Amicable describes the tone of an interaction, agreement, or relationship, not a person's everyday personality -- for that, use affable instead. You'd call a divorce amicable, but a host affable.
